name: Grand Dining Hall, Welcomhotel The Savoy
why_it_matters: The main dining room of Mussoorie's most storied hotel — built in 1902 in English Gothic style, acquired by ITC's Fortune in 2009 and now operated as Welcomhotel by ITC. The Savoy hosted the Princess of Wales (later Queen Mary) in 1906, Pandit Nehru, and the Dalai Lama, and inspired Agatha Christie's first novel after the unsolved 1911 poisoning of Lady Garnet Orme on the property.
insider_tip: The buffet is open to non-residents; book ahead for Sunday lunch on the lawn. Walk the corridors after — the heritage walk past the Writer's Bar and chapel is part of the experience.
signature_address: The Mall, Library Chowk, Mussoorie 248179, Uttarakhand

name: The Writer's Bar, Welcomhotel The Savoy
why_it_matters: The colonial-era bar inside The Savoy — wood-panelled, mountain-view, named for the writers who lived and drank here (Ruskin Bond is a regular patron in the town; Rudyard Kipling and Jim Corbett both passed through the property). Open noon to 11pm.
insider_tip: Sit on the verandah side at sunset — the Doon Valley falls away below. Walk-in works most evenings, but the bar fills up when conferences are in-house.
signature_address: The Mall, Library Chowk, Mussoorie 248179, Uttarakhand

name: The Pavilion, Claridges Nabha Residence
why_it_matters: All-day dining inside the 1830 summer residence of the Maharaja of Nabha — set on 13 acres of cedar-and-oak forest, the only Mussoorie property with private forest. Walls carry archival photographs of British officers, Nawabs and Rajahs who were entertained here.
insider_tip: Non-residents can book a meal — call ahead, it's a 20-minute drive from the Mall. Pair with a heritage walk of the estate; ask for the Victorian Bar afterwards for a cocktail.

name: The Victorian Bar, Claridges Nabha Residence
why_it_matters: Colonial-furniture bar lined with portraits of the erstwhile Nabha rulers — a small, atmospheric room inside the 1830 summer residence. One of two Mussoorie bars (alongside The Savoy's Writer's) where the colonial-officer aesthetic isn't a theme, it's the actual room.
insider_tip: Open to non-residents but call ahead — the bar is small and the property is residential-first.

name: Regency, Jaypee Residency Manor
why_it_matters: The five-star main restaurant at Jaypee Residency Manor — 360-degree glass-fronted room with the cleanest panoramic Doon Valley view in town. Has its own in-house bakery; the bread basket is the unannounced reason regulars return.
insider_tip: Lunch service is the cheaper way in — dinner is set-menu and runs ₹3,000+ per head. Book a window-side table at sunset.

name: Wisteria Deck, JW Marriott Walnut Grove
why_it_matters: Open-air Italian/Mediterranean deck at the JW Marriott — the only Mussoorie restaurant doing serious wood-fired pizza and handmade pasta with locally foraged Himalayan herbs. The deck is glass-screened so it works through monsoon.
insider_tip: It's 17 km out of central Mussoorie en route to Kempty — drive up for sunset, dinner, and stay over, or book in clusters since you've already covered the road.
signature_address: Village Siya, Kempty Falls Road, Mussoorie 248179, Uttarakhand

name: Trout House Grill & Bar, JW Marriott Walnut Grove
why_it_matters: JW Marriott's Indian fine-dining outlet — tandoor and grill with Himalayan twists, including the namesake Himalayan trout cooked tandoori-style. The most polished Indian menu in Mussoorie's hotel circuit.
insider_tip: If you're staying central, club a Wisteria + Trout dinner — the same property handles both, so you get one drive instead of two on the Kempty road.
signature_address: Village Siya, Kempty Falls Road, Mussoorie 248179, Uttarakhand
